newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's left-wing leader stands down for inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's left-wing leader stands down for inquiry.

text.p: The leader of Brazil's biggest opposition party will stand down while allegations he was involved in corruption are investigated, a party spokesman said on Thursday.

Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, honorary president of the Workers Party (PT) and runner-up in Brazil's two most recent presidential elections, will temporarily leave the party's national directorate, the spokesman said. "He wants to make sure the investigations are completely impartial," he added.

An internal PT committee was due to look into claims by a former party official that municipalities controlled by the party hired a consulting firm run by a friend of Lula without considering other bids. In a latest of a string of corruption allegations to rock Brazilian politics, the official also said money paid to the firm found its way back into PT coffers.
Lula has denied the allegations. Party officials said the claims may have come to light now to distract from another alleged corruption scandal involving a government minister.
